title: Fail closed on unresolved OpenCode mutation projections
description: Production blocker found by release review: protocol mismatch and projection statuses unsupported, invalid, or stale can reach execution without a denial; unknown custom or MCP mutators also contradict the declared unknown-effect-deny contract.
acceptance_criteria: Executable CLI and generated-plugin tests prove every unresolved mutating projection is blocked while known read-only tools remain available; full tests and type gates pass.

title: Add a version-gated OpenCode repair-required gate
description: A post-tool finding currently affects only the current call, and sessions sharing a worktree can mutate the same files. OpenCode has one documented hard control point, tool.execute.before, which can throw before mutation, but it exposes no side-effect classification for arbitrary/custom/MCP tools. Persist repair state by worktree/repository generation, use sessionID/callID as provenance, and enforce a deny-by-default pending policy that permits only known read-only and explicit repair/verification tools. Experimental model-context transforms remain optional guidance.
design: Authoritative state lives outside chat history and is keyed by worktree/repository or affected-path generation. While pending, documented tool.execute.before allows known read-only tools plus an explicit repair/verification allowlist and denies unknown-effect tools; calls already past before cannot be retroactively blocked. Register an optional documented custom slopgate_verify_repair tool whose execute path verifies the authoritative worktree and clears only the matching generation, without depending on its own hook events. Use system transform only when sessionID is present and capability tests pass; compaction context merely restates state. app.log is diagnostic; toast is TUI-only.
acceptance_criteria: A confirmed quality violation stores REPAIR_REQUIRED for the affected worktree/repository generation with sessionID/callID provenance; all sessions sharing that worktree observe the gate while separate worktrees remain isolated; pending policy allows only known read-only and explicit repair/verification tools and denies unknown-effect tools; a documented custom verification tool can run clean verification and atomically clear only the matching generation; failed/cancelled/partial tools with no after hook cannot silently clear or avoid the gate when independent evidence recorded a violation; events never clear state; system transform skips injection when sessionID is absent and degrades safely when unavailable; compaction only restates pending context; tests cover concurrent sessions, unknown tools, calls already in flight, transform present/absent, headless mode, compaction, generation races, and every clear condition.
notes: T1: before-hook throw/mutation, custom tools, and compaction context are documented at https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/ and /custom-tools/. T2/T3: system transform is typed/wired with optional sessionID but undocumented; messages transform has no sessionID. SDK session.prompt noReply is not assumed safe recursively. Custom verification executes directly and does not rely on before/after hooks for its clear action; headless plugin-tool hook interception remains an independent unresolved regression.
close_reason: Implemented generation-scoped OpenCode repair state, deny-by-default before-tool gate, direct repair verification CLI/custom tool, compaction restatement, and focused/full validation.

title: Normalize OpenCode tool results and mutation outcomes
description:
Official OpenCode types define tool.execute.before as input {tool, sessionID, callID} plus mutable output.args, and tool.execute.after as input {tool, sessionID, callID, args} plus output {title, output, metadata}. The current shim reads nonexistent output.result and maintains an argument cache even though after receives final args directly. Normalize the documented/typed fields and represent execution and mutation outcomes without inferring success or commit from hook presence or output text.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run OpenCode 1.18.19 with the current Slopgate plugin and execute Read plus apply_patch.
2. Inspect results.jsonl for tool.execute.after rows.
3. Observe tool_output is null because the shim reads output.result instead of output.output.
4. Observe the shim caches args by tool plus cwd despite input.args, sessionID, and callID being available on the typed after hook.
design: Use the official typed hook objects directly. Mutate output.args in place before execution; hook return values are ignored. Model two independent axes: execution_outcome {returned, failed, blocked, cancelled, unknown} and mutation_outcome {committed, partial, none, unknown}, each with evidence_tier. Receiving after proves only normal return on pinned/tested versions; it never proves commit. After-output mutation is source-observed but undocumented and is not a critical delivery channel.
acceptance_criteria: The shim no longer reads output.result or uses the tool-plus-cwd argument cache on supported OpenCode versions; before uses output.args and after uses input.args plus output.title/output/output.metadata; sessionID and callID are preserved; traces store separate execution_outcome, mutation_outcome, and evidence_tier; after receipt may classify execution as returned only on pinned/tested versions and never classifies mutation as committed; absence of after remains unknown because it cannot distinguish block, failure, cancellation, or partial side effects; guidance never says an edit landed without commit evidence; tests cover normal return, thrown/absent after, in-place argument mutation, ignored return values, raw after output, and uncertain/partial mutation.
notes: Evidence tiers: T1 docs https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/ and https://opencode.ai/docs/tools/#apply_patch; T2 Hooks types at anomalyco/opencode commit 3a4c253 packages/plugin/src/index.ts; T3 v1.18.19 execution wrapper commit 2b72179 packages/opencode/src/session/tools.ts. Local eight-event trace recorded null output.result. apply_patch uses tool ID apply_patch and output.args.patchText per official tools docs.
close_reason: Implemented typed OpenCode before/after fields, removed argument correlation cache, preserved native IDs and raw after output, added independent execution/mutation evidence traces, and passed focused plus integration validation.

title: Make OpenCode contract identity adaptive
description: Replace the stale hard-coded OpenCode tool-contract fingerprint with an adaptive, provenance-backed value that follows the active installed/runtime plugin version without network lookups on hook paths. Update tests and benchmark evidence.
design: Decouple Slopgate's private OpenCode projection protocol from OpenCode release numbers. Preserve runtime/declared/lock/installed OpenCode versions as install identity. Emit and require a stable Slopgate-owned projection marker; change it only when the projected payload schema changes. Unknown/mismatched markers remain unsupported. Benchmark reports the stable marker while versions reports OpenCode identity.

Final focused suite: 75 passed. Benchmark: p50 790.903 ms, p95 812.270 ms, decision/finding parity true, fingerprint slopgate-opencode-projection-v1.

title: Reconcile OpenCode enforcement Beads with upstream contracts
description: Audit the eight OpenCode enforcement follow-up Beads against current official OpenCode documentation, installed SDK types, and upstream runtime source. Classify every capability claim by evidence tier, remove unsupported assumptions, and update issue scope, acceptance criteria, dependencies, or priority where necessary.
design: Official docs define supported public capability; tagged upstream source resolves undocumented runtime sequencing; installed types establish the local contract; local probes establish only observed behavior for that version and scenario. Do not generalize one evidence tier into another.
acceptance_criteria: Each OpenCode Bead distinguishes official documentation, upstream source behavior, local observation, and unresolved behavior; unsupported response-shape, blocking, session, cwd, notification, headless, and version assumptions are corrected; capabilities Slopgate can safely leverage are reflected in acceptance criteria; bd lint passes and the reconciliation issue records a claim-by-claim disposition.
notes:
RECONCILIATION METHOD: T1 official opencode.ai docs, T2 official Hooks/Event/config types, T3 pinned upstream source behavior, U unresolved/undocumented. Reviewed current docs on 2026-08-21, OpenCode v1.18.19 SHA 2b72179, current dev SHA 3a4c253, installed plugin types 1.18.5, local traces, and Oracle architecture review.

CONFIRMED PUBLIC CAPABILITIES: tool.execute.before mutates output.args in place and throws to block; plugin context provides directory/worktree; custom tools are documented; compaction context is documented; app.log is the supported plugin log path; run/serve/--pure and CLI --version are documented; /global/health exposes version.

TYPED OR SOURCE-SCOPED ONLY: tool hooks provide sessionID/callID; after input includes args and output is title/output/metadata; system transform is experimental with optional sessionID while messages transform has none; generic events are directory-filtered fire-and-forget; typed hooks are awaited sequentially for pinned versions; after-output mutation works by reference but is undocumented; permission.ask is declared but has no trigger site; headless source wires plugin tools but issue #41422 remains unresolved.

CORRECTED ASSUMPTIONS: removed output.result and after-args omission premises; removed tool/cwd argument cache design; rejected undocumented input.cwd/event.cwd and use directory/worktree; corrected event envelope to properties and file.edited path to properties.file; changed repair authority from session to worktree/repository generation; made sessionID/callID provenance; hard pending gate denies unknown-effect tools and allows known read-only plus explicit repair/verification tools; added documented custom verification tool for generation-checked clear; separated execution and mutation outcomes with evidence tier; missing after remains unknown for block/failure/cancel/partial side effects; generic events are provisional append-only evidence and never clear state; system transform/compaction are advisory enhancements; no headless toast assumption; no nonexistent SDK version method; removed arbitrary 2-second upstream latency assumption; excluded dead permission.ask; preserved plugin-tool headless as unresolved probe.

UPDATED: slopgate-avs, slopgate-4mi, slopgate-ec8, slopgate-66p, slopgate-11o, slopgate-84h, slopgate-vyv, slopgate-deq. slopgate-84h now requires fixture/public-doc refresh and evidence-tier labels.
close_reason: Official-doc, official-type, pinned-source, local-observation, and Oracle reconciliation complete; all eight OpenCode follow-up Beads corrected and scoped to supported capabilities.

title: Pin and expose OpenCode runtime identity
description: The active environment combines OpenCode 1.18.19, installed @opencode-ai/plugin 1.18.5, a stale bun.lock entry for 1.2.27, PATH Slopgate 2.1.5, and source-venv Slopgate 2.1.6. OpenCode publishes the plugin package in lockstep with the CLI, but exposes runtime version through the CLI and raw /global/health endpoint rather than a plugin SDK version method. Establish a reproducible install identity without inventing unavailable client fields.
design: At install/diagnostic time, collect OpenCode from opencode --version or raw /global/health, plugin SDK version from its package.json/lock, and Slopgate version plus resolved binary path. Record the snapshot timestamp and provenance in trace metadata; do not perform a health request per hook. Keep app.log as the documented server-side logging channel. Treat engines.opencode compatibility checks as source-supported, not a docs guarantee.
acceptance_criteria: The installer selects one explicit Slopgate binary; package.json, lockfile, and installed @opencode-ai/plugin agree or diagnostics report stale installation; OpenCode runtime version comes from documented CLI output or the health endpoint, not a nonexistent SDK method; plugin-load metadata records runtime/package/Slopgate versions with provenance, resolved binary, plugin-instance ID, directory, and worktree; per-hook traces separately record native sessionID, callID, hook name, execution/mutation evidence, and generation; diagnostics distinguish compatible skew from stale files and identify restart/reinstall steps; app.log works headless and no criterion relies on TUI toast visibility. No redaction behavior is part of this task.
notes:
T1: https://opencode.ai/docs/cli/ documents --version; https://opencode.ai/docs/server/#global documents GET /global/health; Plugins docs require client.app.log instead of console output. T3: plugin and CLI packages are lockstep at v1.18.19/current dev, and npm plugin engines.opencode is checked by the loader. Local Hooks types are unchanged across observed 1.18.x despite stale versions.
2026-08-22 completion: aligned OpenCode runtime, declared, Bun lock, and installed @opencode-ai/plugin at 1.18.21. Fixed Bun JSONC lock parsing and added regression coverage. Live identity API reports compatible/remediation=none. Ten-run benchmark: p50 752.301 ms, p95 793.247 ms, parity true, under 1000/1250 ms SLO.
close_reason: OpenCode install identity is aligned and observable; Bun lock parsing, regression coverage, live identity QA, and latency benchmark all pass.

title: Use native OpenCode identity and eliminate arg/cwd correlation state
description:
OpenCode's typed tool hooks already provide sessionID and callID, and tool.execute.after provides final args. Plugin initialization provides stable directory and worktree. Tool-hook inputs and generic event envelopes do not provide cwd. Replace synthetic canonical identity, mutable currentDirectory, and tool-plus-cwd argument caching with the native contract; parse event identity from event.properties and the file.edited path from properties.file.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start concurrent OpenCode sessions or subagents in one plugin instance and invoke the same tool.
2. Inspect hook inputs and Slopgate traces.
3. Observe native sessionID/callID/final args exist but the shim records one generated session ID and correlates via tool plus mutable cwd.
4. Emit file.edited and observe the official properties.file key is not among the shim path keys.
design: For typed hooks, pass input.sessionID, input.callID, and input.args/output.args directly. Use plugin-context directory/worktree as the authoritative filesystem scope and shell.env.cwd only on that typed hook. Repair state is keyed by worktree/repository or affected-path generation; sessionID/callID are provenance, not isolation boundaries. For generic events read fields from event.properties. Delete mutable cwd and argument-cache state rather than re-keying it.
acceptance_criteria: Tool hooks use native sessionID/callID and direct typed args with no tool/cwd cache; canonical repo scope uses plugin directory/worktree and never undocumented input.cwd or event.cwd; authoritative repair state is shared by sessions operating on the same worktree and isolated across different worktrees; concurrent state changes are generation-checked or atomic; shell.env may supply cwd only from its typed input; generic events read session identity from properties and file.edited reads properties.file; compatibility/native duplicates are deduplicated without collapsing distinct calls or worktrees.
notes: Evidence: official Plugins docs document plugin context directory/worktree; official Hooks types expose sessionID/callID and after input.args but no cwd on tool hooks; Event is {id,type,properties}; v1.18.19 source filters events to the plugin directory before delivery. Current local shim lines 118-147, 306-352, and 425+ use generated identity/cache/mutable cwd.
close_reason: Implemented native OpenCode sessionID/callID propagation, direct typed args, event.properties parsing, stable worktree scope, and scoped atomic hook state; focused and affected suites pass.

title: Use typed OpenCode hooks for control and generic events for telemetry
description:
OpenCode generic event handlers return Promise<void> but v1.18.19/current source invokes them fire-and-forget; they cannot block originating work or safely author ordered lifecycle transitions. The event envelope is {id,type,properties}. Slopgate currently attempts enforcement from file.edited and treats several event fields as top-level. Reserve hard control for documented tool.execute.before and use generic events only for append-only telemetry, provisional mutation evidence, lifecycle observations, and human notification.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Perform a file mutation that emits file.edited and a blocking quality result.
2. Trace the generic event handler and upstream dispatch.
3. Observe upstream discards the event promise while Slopgate throws from the event path.
4. Observe official event data is nested under properties and file.edited uses properties.file.
design: Never throw from event. Catch and log event-handler failures. Generic events are append-only telemetry and provisional evidence: they cannot clear repair state, supersede newer verification, or author authoritative lifecycle transitions without generation reconciliation. Use typed, wired tool.execute.before for control; do not rely on permission.ask because it is declared but has no trigger site. Treat permission event names as version-sensitive. Keep file.edited as delayed directory-scoped evidence, not rollback or denial.
acceptance_criteria: Generic event handling is telemetry/advisory only and never throws for policy control; event fields are read from properties, including file.edited.file and session IDs; rejected or reordered event work is caught and logged; event evidence is generation-tagged and cannot clear or overwrite authoritative repair state; hard mutation control is owned by tool.execute.before; no path depends on permission.ask or one permission event spelling; capability docs distinguish typed chat.message from a documented prompt blocker; tests prove event-side findings do not masquerade as tool denial, do not clear newer state, and preserve provisional mutation evidence.
notes: T1 docs list generic events and use them for notifications. T2 Event handler returns Promise<void>. T3 v1.18.19 commit 2b72179 and current dev 3a4c253 invoke void hook.event after directory filtering. permission.ask is typed but an exhaustive source scan found no trigger site; permission event names diverge across docs and schemas.
close_reason: Typed tool.execute.before remains the hard control point; generic events now catch/log failures, file.edited is advisory provisional evidence, docs clarify prompt/permission limitations, and Bun plus state/trace contract tests pass.

title: Add an OpenCode hook contract regression matrix
description: Current tests cover adapter shapes and installer text but not the real OpenCode plugin lifecycle or evidence-tier boundaries. Add executable tests for documented hook behavior, typed-but-experimental features, source-only behavior, and unresolved headless plugin-tool behavior so Slopgate never upgrades an observation into a public contract.
design: Separate four layers: official-doc contract tests, official Hooks/Event type fixtures, pinned-version integration tests for source-confirmed sequencing, and live smoke probes. The matrix must label experimental/source-only assertions and produce an explicit compatibility diagnostic when they change.
acceptance_criteria: The matrix covers before-hook in-place args mutation and throw-to-block; ignored hook return values; after input.args and output.title/output/metadata; missing after after throw/cancel/partial side effect; separate execution/mutation/evidence axes; absence of output.result and hook cwd; native sessionID/callID; worktree-scoped state shared across sessions and isolated across worktrees; generation races; event {id,type,properties}, directory filtering, delayed/reordered file.edited.file, and append-only advisory behavior; permission.ask declared-but-untriggered negative coverage; system-transform sessionID present/absent and graceful fallback; compaction advisory context; deny-by-default unknown-effect tool policy; custom verification tool generation-checked clearing independent of hook interception; headless run with plugins, --pure control, built-in hooks, and plugin-tool regression probe; headless app.log versus TUI-only toast; stale version identity; harness_schema_context.json and public capability docs are refreshed; every case labels documented, typed, pinned-source, local-observed, or unresolved evidence.
notes: Headless run/serve/--pure are documented. v1.18.19 source wires the full plugin layer and registry tools, but anomalyco/opencode#41422 reports plugin-tool hooks missing in a long 1.18.15 headless loop; keep this unresolved. Pinned integration cases must cover a tool that throws after a side effect, cross-session same-worktree gating, unknown custom/MCP tools, event reordering, and system transform without sessionID. Source fixtures: v1.18.19 SHA 2b72179; current review 3a4c253.
close_reason: Added machine-validated OpenCode lifecycle matrix with evidence tiers, live Bun control tests, schema/docs linkage, stale identity property coverage, and clean focused/lint validation.

title: Audit OpenCode hook enforcement findings
description: Investigate the reported OpenCode Slopgate shim contract, repair-gate, event-dispatch, identity/correlation, cwd, runtime-version, headless-dispatch, and regression-test claims. Record evidence-backed dispositions and create deduplicated follow-up Beads only for confirmed actionable gaps.
acceptance_criteria: Each reported claim has a confirmed, disproved, or unresolved disposition with source/upstream evidence; every confirmed actionable gap is represented by a non-duplicate Bead with acceptance criteria; the audit Bead is closed when the inventory is complete.
notes: CONFIRMED: (1) OpenCode tool-result contract mismatch: shim reads output.result while SDK 1.18.5/runtime 1.18.19 expose title/output/metadata; traces recorded null outputs. Follow-up slopgate-avs. (2) Post-tool quality guidance can claim an edit landed without mutation evidence; use explicit execution and mutation states. slopgate-avs. (3) Blocking post-tool errors affect only the current call; no durable model-facing repair state exists. slopgate-4mi. (4) Native sessionID/callID are ignored, arguments are cached by tool plus cwd, and mutable global cwd can misattribute concurrent sessions/worktrees; native and compatibility traces can duplicate. slopgate-ec8. (5) Generic event dispatch is fire-and-forget upstream, so file.edited cannot be a reliable enforcement boundary. slopgate-66p. (6) Runtime identity is split across OpenCode 1.18.19, plugin package 1.18.5, PATH Slopgate 2.1.5, venv Slopgate 2.1.6, and stale lock/install state. slopgate-11o. (7) Mutation evaluations measured 7142-7415 ms versus millisecond read-only evaluations. slopgate-vyv. (8) Full lifecycle/headless/concurrency contract coverage is missing. slopgate-84h. (9) Post-tool rejection is inherently late; safe projected preflight is an actionable enhancement for deterministic edits. slopgate-deq. NOT REPRODUCED: a general opencode run hook bypass; a local OpenCode 1.18.19 built-in Read probe fired both before/after hooks. UNRESOLVED/NARROW: the upstream plugin-provided-tool headless scenario remains open and belongs in slopgate-84h, not a standalone confirmed bug. Also, partial mutation cannot be inferred from current host data and must remain mutation_unknown unless evidence proves otherwise. Eight deduplicated follow-up Beads created with acceptance criteria and dependencies.
close_reason: Audit complete: all claims dispositioned and eight confirmed actionable gaps captured as follow-up Beads.

description: Trace and prove the stable Slopgate-owned projection marker from install command through rendered OpenCode plugin to Python projection enforcement; fix any broken seam and validate an actual generated installation.
notes: Verified command routing: CLI install -> install_platform -> install_opencode -> render_opencode_plugin -> scoped file write. Targeted suite: 46 passed. Manual QA used XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/opencode/slopgate-installer-wiring-20260822; install exited 0, generated plugin contained resolved binary, populated install identity, and slopgate-opencode-projection-v1. Bun imported the generated file and instantiated EnforcerPlugin with before/after/event handlers and slopgate.plugin.loaded log.

title: Reduce OpenCode mutation hook latency
description: Local traces measured about 7.1-7.4 seconds for apply_patch post-tool evaluation while read-only events took milliseconds. OpenCode provides no documented hook latency, timeout, ordering, or concurrency SLO. Tagged source shows typed hooks are awaited inside tool execution, so Slopgate evaluation time directly affects observed tool latency for the pinned versions. Profile and optimize Slopgate without presenting an arbitrary threshold as an upstream contract.
design: Measure dispatch, subprocess startup, rule-engine, collector, and trace phases separately. Define a Slopgate-owned interactive SLO only after a reproducible baseline and representative repository sample. Preserve policy and finding parity; do not move blocking work to generic events or skip collectors to improve latency.
acceptance_criteria: A benchmark records per-phase mutation-hook latency, repository size, touched content, OpenCode version, plugin version, and Slopgate version; the dominant cost is identified; maintainers set and document a Slopgate-owned target from the baseline rather than assuming a 2-second upstream contract; optimization materially improves p50/p95 while preserving findings and decisions; caches include content, repo, policy, and tool-contract fingerprints; traces expose phase timing and tests prove awaited control remains on the typed hook path.
notes: Completed 2026-08-22. Added reproducible awaited OpenCode mutation benchmark with repository/content/tool-contract/policy fingerprints and phase timing; documented Slopgate-owned p50 <=1000ms and p95 <=1250ms targets; optimized collector parsing with request-local cache/timing while preserving typed-hook awaited control and decision/finding parity. Final live 10-run result after 2 warmups: p50 818.187ms, p95 901.323ms, dominant evaluation_ms, decision_parity=true, finding_parity=true. Verification: 2377 passed, 8 skipped; slopgate lint check --details --profile reports no violations; targeted basedpyright and Ruff clean; benchmark help, invalid-input rejection, and live generated-plugin execution exercised.
close_reason: Acceptance criteria satisfied with passing full suite, clean quality gate, documented SLO, and live parity benchmark under target.

title: Preflight projected quality for supported OpenCode edits
description: Post-tool rejection cannot undo a mutation. OpenCode officially documents tool.execute.before as an in-place argument mutation and throw-to-block surface, and its tools docs specify apply_patch arguments under output.args.patchText. For deterministic mutation tools, construct projected content before execution, run applicable quality checks, and throw only when the projection is trustworthy; retain post-edit observation for everything else.
design: Use documented output.args and exact versioned tool schemas. Start with apply_patch.patchText and other payloads whose resulting content can be reconstructed without filesystem races. Preflight classification is separate from the pending repair gate: while repair is pending, unknown-effect tools are denied unless explicitly allowlisted. Never rely on permission.ask. Unsupported operations fall back to post-tool observation with mutation unknown; file.edited is provisional evidence and cannot clear state. The dedicated verification tool owns authoritative clean clearing.
acceptance_criteria: Supported tool IDs and schemas are versioned, including apply_patch.patchText; deterministic projections do not touch disk and can deny through documented before-hook throw; projections verify current state; unsupported, dynamic, invalid, concurrent-change, custom, MCP, and unknown-effect operations never receive a false safe classification and are denied while a hard repair gate is pending unless explicitly allowlisted; preflight and post-tool findings deduplicate by stable generation-aware identity; tests cover valid/invalid/multi-file apply_patch, write/edit schemas, concurrent changes, unknown tools, missing after after partial side effects, and post-tool fallback; only the dedicated clean verification path may clear repair state; docs state after/file.edited cannot roll back.
notes: T1 evidence: https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/#env-protection and https://opencode.ai/docs/tools/#apply_patch. T3 confirms before executes before item.execute and after after mutation for v1.18.19/current dev. permission.ask is intentionally excluded because it has no trigger site despite its type declaration.
close_reason: Implemented versioned OpenCode mutation projection and fail-closed repair enforcement; full automated validation and live clean/pending/stale/success/corrupt CLI QA passed.
